title: Free time for the whole team
prompt:
Each person has a sorted list of busy [start, end) blocks; return every gap of positive length when nobody is busy, between the earliest start and the latest end.

- schedules has 0 to 10,000 people and at most 100,000 blocks in total, with integers 0 <= start < end <= 10^9.
- One person's blocks are sorted by start and never overlap (they may touch). A person's list may be empty.
- Blocks are end-exclusive, so [1, 3] and [3, 5] leave no gap between them.
- Return maximal free slots as [start, end] pairs sorted by start. Ignore time before the first busy block and after the last; return [] if nobody is ever busy.
hints: Who is busy doesn't matter, only whether anyone is. Think of all the blocks as one combined list.
Process every block in order of start time while tracking the latest end seen so far.
When a block starts after that latest end, [latestEnd, start] is a free slot. Then update latestEnd = max(latestEnd, end).

solution.explanation: A moment is free for everyone exactly when it lies outside the union of all busy blocks, so the problem reduces to merging intervals and reporting the gaps. Sweeping blocks by start while tracking the latest end merges the union on the fly; any start beyond that end opens a gap. The strict > keeps touching blocks from producing zero-length slots.

complexity.notes: N is the total number of blocks. Since each person's list is already sorted, a k-way merge with a min-heap brings this to O(N log k) for k people.

followUps: Use the per-person sorting: merge the lists with a heap in O(N log k).
Only return free slots at least d minutes long that fall within working hours [open, close).
